Welcome to Culvers House Primary School
We are a two form entry Primary School located in Sutton, close to the Merton border. As an inclusive, community school we believe that every child deserves the best possible education in a supportive and challenging setting. Staff and children work together to create a learning environment in which everyone can flourish and achieve their full potential, both academically and socially. We have developed a vibrant curriculum, filled with many rich and stimulating learning experiences. We have high expectations of all of our pupils and are rightly proud of our high standards.
Our school values underpin our school ethos:

We welcome visits to see us in action. Please phone our School Office on 020 8255 6199 to make an appointment.

English Reading at Culvers House Primary School
Reading is at the heart of the curriculum at Culvers House Primary School; we place great importance on the value of reading and actively promote it at every opportunity. It is an essential skill that will enable the children to develop emotionally, culturally and socially, ensuring that they flourish in our diverse society. Our Reading intention is to provide a diverse and rich curriculum that equips all pupils with the skills to read with fluency, comprehension and prosody.
As part of the Little Wandle phonics programme, in Reception and Year 1, reading practice sessions take place three times a week, allowing the children to develop their reading skills and vocabulary knowledge. In Year 2 and in KS2, children participate in weekly whole class Guided Reading sessions. During this time, comprehension skills are taught explicitly, using a variety of shorter extracts and written responses.
We value the importance of nurturing a passion for reading and encourage the children to choose a variety of books regularly. In addition to reading books at their appropriate reading level, children are also encouraged to choose a book of their choice, which they can enjoy and share with others at home.
Story time is part of our daily timetable. The children enjoy listening to an adult model reading with fluency and prosody. Carefully selected stories, spanning a range of genres, diverse plots and characters, ensure that the children experience a range of topics. Promoting a culture of enthusiastic readers is further supported by providing reading events, such as book fairs, World Book Day and World Poetry Day celebrations.

Music at Culvers House Primary School
Music can help to develop the skills, attitudes and attributes that can support learning in other national curriculum subjects. This includes listening skills, the ability to concentrate, creativity, intuition, sensitivity, perseverance, the ability to work in a group, self-confidence and sensitivity towards others.
Music is taught weekly so that children learn the sound and meaning of a piece of music while appreciating a variety of different styles. Children will be able to explore and experiment, developing a love and appreciation for the subject.
At Culvers House Primary School, we follow the Charanga scheme of work. The scheme supports all the requirements of the national curriculum and provides a practical and exploratory approach to musical learning, which our children really enjoy. Each unit of work comprises of the different strands of musical learning which correspond with the national curriculum for music, including: Understanding music; Listening and Responding; Musical Activities (including warm-up games, singing, playing instruments, Improvisation, Composing, Performing). As part of the curriculum, we offer Whole Class Ensemble Tuition to learn the guitar for all pupils in Year 4. We also have individual guitar and piano lessons available to our Key Stage 2 pupils. Each week, the children take part in singing assemblies for both Key Stage 1 and 2.

Art and Design at Culvers House Primary School
At Culvers House Primary School, we have created an art curriculum which is exciting, rich and inspires children to express their individual creativity. We encourage sharing and exploring through Art and Design, which enables children to be creative while also learning key skills. Art and Design is a practical subject, where children have regular experiences and exposure to a diverse range of artists so they can understand historical and cultural development in art. They will also learn to evaluate, analyse and appreciate their own and others’ artwork and develop an awareness that the process of creating art is equally as valuable as the finished product.

Computing at Culvers House Primary School
At Culvers House Primary School, we follow a Computing curriculum informed by the National Curriculum, Development Matters (2021) guidance and our Culvers House EYFS Curriculum, using resources and inspiration from the Teach Computing and Kapow curricula. Computing is taught discretely, in weekly hour-long lessons, in addition to Online Safety lessons, which take place during carefully planned and sequenced P.S.H.E. lessons. During Computing lessons, children are given opportunities to use a range of technologies, including Beebots, iPads, Chromebooks and Microbits. Using these technologies, children are then taught how to apply a range of skills, through project-based learning, including tasks such as: creating word documents, programming a game, making collaborative presentations, writing blogs, and creating stop-frame animations. As well as practising key IT skills, children build on their knowledge each year, learning about different uses for IT, databases, networks, search technologies to allow them to become responsible digital citizens in a technologically evolving world. A range of strategies are used to engage pupils and deepen their understanding of new concepts: live coding, skill modelling, paired programming, vocabulary modelling, and the use of stories and videos as prompts for e-safety discussions. The concepts and skills taught in Computing are assessed formatively using opportunities such as peer and self-assessment, self-reflection, quizzes, posters and verbal questioning.

English Writing at Culvers House Primary School
At Culvers House Primary School, we strongly believe it is essential to equip children in written and spoken English, including: grammatical construction, spelling and oracy (the ability to take part a conversation as well as develop vocabulary understanding). This belief underpins the English curriculum and it can also be seen reflected and applied throughout the broader curriculum.
Writing is taught explicitly, through high-quality teacher modelling, as well as through the exploration of rich texts, which underpin learning in all areas of the curriculum. Through the four writing purposes (Entertain, Inform, Discuss and Persuade) children learn how words can be used and manipulated to convey meaning effectively. Where possible, they also have the opportunity to write for real-life purposes, so that they see the impact of their efforts.
The English learning journey is divided into a clear structure, which begins with exploring model texts and gathering ideas. Following this, children then have the opportunity to plan and write their own pieces, before proof-reading and editing these based on feedback from their teachers. By the end of each unit, children feel a sense of accomplishment in being able to publish their writing in their publishing book, which follows them across Key Stage 2 and showcases the excellent progress they have made within their writing journey.
Teachers use rigorous assessment for learning as lesson sequences progress, giving instant feedback to tailor the experience to the children and their needs. We also purposely build in opportunities to revisit skills, to support committing them to children’s long term and working memory and skill set.

History at Culvers House Primary School
History plays a crucial role at Culvers House. We encourage our children to think and act like historians by building their knowledge and understanding of people, events and contexts from a range of historical periods, covering the world, British and local history. Children have opportunities to think critically about events and communicate ideas to a range of audiences in a variety of ways. Our aim is to make History practical, thought-provoking and accessible to all pupils. Learning about the past should stimulate curiosity and questioning, and shape the children’s views, attitudes and values for the future.
Our carefully sequenced history curriculum is shaped around the common threads of trade, society, settlement and power. Regular opportunities are identified for children to review prior learning and make meaningful links between different aspects of history. A main enquiry question drives each topic at Culvers House. Our focus on historical enquiry supports children of all ages and abilities to become enthusiastic, active learners through posing their own questions and discussing how to go about finding answers, using a range of historical sources. Our intent is for every child to feel confident in their understanding of the past, its impact on the present, and its consequence for the future.

Maths at Culvers House Primary School
At Culvers House Primary School, we aim to develop positive and confident mathematicians. Our curriculum enables children to:
be taught the skills to problem solve
develop reasoning skills to enable them to discuss and evaluate different mathematical concepts
link mathematical concepts to real-life situations.
Culvers House follows a Mastery approach to teaching Maths. This emphasises the importance of children gaining a deep and secure understanding of a concept or procedure before moving on to the next stage of their learning. For this reason, our curriculum is organised into units, with learning moving on when children are ready. Our curriculum is also designed to be cumulative, so that once a topic is covered it is met many times again in different contexts. For example, place value is always taught as the first unit in Autumn 1, but is revisited in other units, including ‘Addition and Subtraction’, ‘Multiplication and Division’ and ‘Measure’. Prior learning is also revised and revisited through use of mental starters at the beginning of each lesson.
Mathematical understanding is developed through a concrete-pictorial-abstract (CPA) approach. Use of representations are first of all concrete (e.g. dienes, counters, beads), then pictorial (e.g. array, drawing place value counters) to then facilitate abstract working (e.g. columnar addition, long multiplication). This approach enables the children to develop strong mathematical fluency. Methods and progression for the CPA approach are outlined in our Calculation Policy for Years 1-6. Problem solving and reasoning activities are a key part of every lesson and children are encouraged to explain their ideas, observations and methods.
Our lessons are designed with the aim that children move together at the same pace. In order to ensure children are provided with appropriate challenge, independent tasks and parts of whole class teaching are differentiated so that all children can achieve. Alongside their teachers, children are encouraged to make appropriate choices about which task they should challenge themselves with. Where additional support is required, same-day ‘Keep-Up’ interventions are delivered by teaching assistants, so that children are ready to move on to the next stage of their learning.

P.E. at Culvers House Primary School
The P.E. curriculum at Culvers House Primary School focuses on fundamental movement skills, encouraging children to become increasingly competent and confident in their agility, balance and coordination as well as strength, flexibility, technique and control. It also has a key emphasis on developing every child’s intrapersonal skills such as self-belief, resilience, sportsmanship/ respect and teamwork.
Our curriculum incorporates two approaches to maximise the development of these targeted skills. We follow the REAL P.E. approach in one of our P.E. lessons, with each half-term focusing on one of the subsequent areas:
In the other P.E. lesson of each week, we utilise the Merton P.E. scheme for Games, Dance, Gymnastics, Athletics and OAA topics. This approach provides opportunities for the children to take part in a range of sports and disciplines, where they can build on the skills developed in the Real P.E. lesson whilst learning more sport specific skills, rules and strategies. Personal and interpersonal competition is woven into each unit of learning. Physically active lessons that promote an enjoyment of exercise, games and sport underpin every lesson.
We are a member of the Sutton School Sports Partnership (SSSP) and with their support we aim to provide further opportunities to experience local competitions against other schools. Local festivals are also planned into the P.E. calendar to allow children to develop new interests in sports within the community.
Throughout the year, there are also a range of extra-curricular clubs available to attend such as: Chelsea Football Club, Street Dance, Multi-sports and Tennis.
At Culvers House, our Year 5 children attend their swimming lessons at Westcroft Leisure Centre. Each swimming lesson is delivered by a qualified swimming instructor and the children partake in a progressive program that teaches the children to swim using different strokes.

PSHE (Personal, Social and Health Education) and RSE (Relationships and Sex Education) at Culvers House Primary School
At Culvers House Primary School, we believe that children should grow into mature, resilient, open-minded, lifelong learners. We have developed our PSHE and RSE curriculum by centering it around The National Curriculum, Development Matters (2021) and our Culvers House EYFS curriculum, in order to ensure full coverage and carefully sequencing. In PSHE, each year group from Years 1-6 focus on the key strands: Rights and Responsibilities, Identity, Safety and Risk, Health and Money and The Working World. Similarly, in RSHE, each year group from Years 1-6 focus on the key strands: Online Relationships and Relationships/Friendships. Additionally, Year 5 learn about Puberty as part of the Science curriculum and Year 6 receive appropriate Sex Education lessons. Our PSHE and RSE lessons are taught weekly in every year group. Within the lessons, the children focus on using meaningful dialogue, role-play and circle times to discuss their experiences, scenarios, feelings and opinions. The teachers use a wide range of resources from Kapow, Young Citizens' Primary Resources and 1Decsion to inform their planning and ensure that the children are stimulated and engaged in their PSHE and RSE lessons. All learning is evidenced in each class’ floor book, which includes: quotes and discussions from the children and staff, photos from the children’s role-play or circle times, any group activities that the children complete and post-it notes including the children’s opinions and thoughts.

R.E. at Culvers House Primary School
At Culvers House Primary School, our aim is to develop our children’s understanding of the world around them so that they are accepting and tolerant individuals with a good understanding of the diverse world that they live in.
During RE lessons, children are given opportunities to develop a deeper understanding of a range of religions and cultures found within their community and beyond and is an excellent opportunity to teach, discuss and reflect on living in a multicultural society.
At Culvers House Primary School, we follow the London Borough of Sutton syllabus for Religious Education (SACRE) which takes into account that Great Britain is traditionally Christian, while also recognising the teachings and practices of other principal religions. RE is taught for one hour on a weekly basis. As well as these discrete RE lessons, other opportunities arise to discuss RE through topics, assemblies and festivals throughout the year.
Children are given the opportunity to develop their curiosity and ask questions, through the use of real life artefacts, trips to local places of worship, and inviting speakers into school from various faith groups. We make learning in RE meaningful by encouraging lots of class and group discussions. Children are also encouraged to discuss their own religious beliefs and share experiences with each other.

Early Years Curriculum at Culvers House Primary School
It is our aim at Culvers House Primary School that every child feels happy, safe and secure, that they develop a lively and enquiring mind and that they fulfil their own potential in learning. We follow the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) framework, which is for children aged from birth to five years. It is a crucial part of children’s education and it should underpin all future learning. At Culvers House Primary School, we have created a culture based around our eight key school values: thoughtfulness, resilience, morality, respect, adaptability, communication, collaboration and enquiry; these thread through every learning experience in school and aim to shape learners who know how to make a positive contribution to their community and the wider society.
At Culvers House Primary School
At Culvers House, the children in the Early Years work cohesively across and within year groups. For example, in Reception the provision is set up as a unit rather than two separate classrooms and the children are able to access all areas. We have regular Early Years assemblies where special events are celebrated as well a ‘Celebration Assembly’ to celebrate the children’s achievements.
We understand that play is an integral part of learning and this is at the heart of our Early Years curriculum. We believe that the correct mix of adult-directed and uninterrupted child-initiated play ensures the best outcomes for pupils. Warm and positive relationships between staff and children, consistent routines and strong relationships with parents are key.
At Culvers House Primary School, we meet the welfare requirements laid down in the Statutory Framework for the Early Years Foundation Stage and actively safeguard and promote the welfare of all of our children.
Our Early Years curriculum is based on story-led learning, which is responsive to the children’s needs and often linked to the children’s current interests. ‘The Overarching Principles of EYFS at Culvers House’ demonstrates how children are treated as individuals and are encouraged to be resilient, capable, confident and self-assured. It shows how children learn to be strong and independent through positive relationships with adults and their peers. The document describes the enabling environments that have been carefully set up in both Nursery and Reception, where the children learn and develop well with teaching and support from adults, who respond to their individual interests and needs and help them to build their learning over time. The learning environments also enable the children to demonstrate the ‘Characteristics of effective teaching and learning’ as detailed in the Early Years Foundation Stage Framework.
We pride ourselves on creating a ‘language-rich’ environment through the use of songs, nursery rhymes, poems, stories and providing time for quality interactions between adults and between peers. Our experienced staff ensure that interactions are positive, allowing children to flourish and gather words at pace in order to become confident communicators. Children are encouraged to become early readers through enjoyment of books and the systematic teaching of phonics through the ‘Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised’ programme.
The children learn nursery rhymes and develop their mathematical thinking through direct teaching and exploration. We want our children to become confident mathematicians who can apply what they have learnt to real life experiences. In Reception, we follow the ‘White Rose Maths’ programme.
We have designed our indoor and outdoor learning environments in a way that promotes both awe and wonder, encourages independent learning and provides challenge. The outdoor areas have equipment that enables our children to strengthen their core muscles through physical play. Our learning environment is adaptable in order to reflect children's interests and progression. The children are supported to learn to work together, manage their feelings and ask questions through skilled adult-facilitated play.
We understand the importance of parental engagement and believe that our parents have a crucial role to play in their children's education. We work hard to create strong partnerships between home and school. Every week, we post the pages from our class scrapbooks on ‘Google Classroom’ and inform parents of the topic that is planned from the following week. We also hold termly ‘Stay and Play’ sessions where the parents are invited to join their children in the classroom setting.
As part of the learning and teaching process, children are assessed in relation to their progress towards the Early Learning Goals (ELGs). These judgements are made on the basis of accumulative observations and in-depth knowledge of the children acquired through ongoing assessments. These ongoing assessments are used to inform planning and next steps in teaching and learning for all children throughout the year.
Children in our Nursery and Reception classes make good progress from their starting points. Our curriculum is inclusive and meets the needs of all children, enabling all children to reach their own potential. During their time with us, children make progress towards the national expectation for a Good Level of Development (GLD) at the end of the year. Children develop their characteristics of learning and are able to apply their knowledge to a range of situations making links and explaining their ideas and understanding. Children are confident to take risks and discuss their successes and failures with peers and adults, drawing on their experiences to improve or adjust what they are doing. We believe our high standards are due to our carefully planned environment, enriched play-based curriculum, quality first teaching and the rigour of assessment.
